title: Files by New York day
prompt: The New York team files every reading under its New York calendar date, not the UTC one. Write `save(observations, path)` so it saves the readings as Parquet with one folder per New York date. `solve` is written for you: it reads the folder back and notes which folder each reading came from.
rules: `local_date` is the date on a New York clock when the reading was taken. `observed_at` is UTC, and New York moved its clocks forward on 2026-03-08.
Save `observation_id`, `station_id`, `observed_at`, `temperature_c` and `local_date`, partitioned by `local_date`, so each reading sits in a folder such as `local_date=2026-03-07`.
The folder may hold an earlier save: replace it.
Keep every reading, repeated rows included. An empty batch saves no folders.
hints: `F.from_utc_timestamp("observed_at", "America/New_York")` shows a UTC time on New York's clock; `F.to_date` keeps the day.
Use the zone's name, not a fixed offset: New York is 5 hours behind UTC before 2026-03-08 07:00 UTC and 4 hours after.
`select` the four columns plus the new date with `alias("local_date")`, then `write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy("local_date").parquet(path)`.
explanation: Work out the New York date with `F.to_date(F.from_utc_timestamp("observed_at", "America/New_York"))`, select it as `local_date` next to the four columns, and save with `.write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy("local_date").parquet(path)`. A reading at 04:00 UTC on 2026-03-08 is still 23:00 on 2026-03-07 in New York, so `observation_date` or `to_date(observed_at)` files it under the wrong day. A fixed offset of -5 hours goes wrong after the clocks change, and saving `local_date` inside the files instead of partitioning by it leaves every reading outside a date folder.
